## Screen: joint tests of each feature set

| family | set | n | k | test | statistic | df | p | robust Wald p | aliased |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ml | situational (schedule, travel, venue, injuries, QB, officials) | 1365 | 29 | LR chi2 | 26.933 | 30 | 0.6268 | 0.4450 | inj_diff_all |
| ml | all point-in-time features incl. model-vs-market | 1365 | 34 | LR chi2 | 35.865 | 36 | 0.4750 | 0.0076 | d_e1 inj_diff_all |
| ats | situational (schedule, travel, venue, injuries, QB, officials) | 1372 | 29 | F | 1.057 | 29 | 0.3838 | 0.0837 | inj_diff_all |
| ats | all point-in-time features incl. model-vs-market | 1372 | 34 | F | 1.180 | 34 | 0.2211 | 0.0000 | d_e1 inj_diff_all |
| tot | situational (schedule, travel, venue, injuries, QB, officials) | 1372 | 29 | F | 1.030 | 29 | 0.4224 | 0.0003 | inj_diff_all |
| tot | all point-in-time features incl. model-vs-market | 1372 | 34 | F | 1.066 | 34 | 0.3672 | 0.0000 | d_e1 inj_diff_all |

The model-based LR/F tests are the primary joint tests. The week-clustered Wald test is shown for completeness: with 29–34 coefficients and about 90 week clusters its covariance estimate is unstable and it over-rejects (Cameron & Miller 2015), so it is not evidence on its own.
